summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — CDW +6%, VLO +5%, CHTR +4%, ORCL +4%, IFF +4%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AMAT -7%, FLEX -6%, JNJ -5%, DPZ -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: AMAT (-7.02%) — Chip-equipment profit-taking after a ~80% YTD run. AMAT gave no industry spending forecast at its investor day, and China/geopolitical worries added to the selling. LRCX and KLA fell about 4%. Date matching is uncertain. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: AMAT is a ~$370B large-cap semi-equipment name that no strategy lists. The drop was a gradual sector de-rating (sixth straight down day) with no gap or catalyst, and a long-only bot has no use for it.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for CDW on 2026-10-14. Search returned only older earnings-driven jumps and undated items, so this is likely a sector or technical move (IT hardware/AI-spend sentiment).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CDW is a mid-cap IT reseller/distributor that no strategy lists. With no identified news catalyst, a news-reactive trigger had nothing to fire on, and a +5.9% close-to-close move gave no pre-market signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe slot to momentum-trader that admits any US name with a close-to-close move ≥ +5% on ≥1.5× average volume and a market cap above a floor (e.g. $5B), instead of relying on a static ticker list.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for 2026-10-14. Likely a sector-wide refiner rally on strong diesel/jet crack spreads, with VLO near record highs after a 2026 run of over 100%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: VLO is a large-cap energy/refining name that no strategy includes. It was also extended near all-time highs, so RSI and extension filters would likely have rejected it even if it had been in a universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap energy refiners (VLO, MPC, PSX) to the momentum universe, with a sector-relative-strength trigger such as a refiner basket up 3% or more on the day, instead of per-name gap/RSI caps that block names already at highs.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Oct 14 catalyst. CHTR rebounded +4.4% to 106.89, just off a 52-week low, ahead of Q3 earnings on Nov 6. Coverage points to a Cox-integration and cost-cut narrative, so likely a technical bounce.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CHTR is a large-cap cable name that no strategy includes. It is also in a long downtrend near 52-week lows, so a momentum or trend filter would have excluded it even if it were in the universe.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap telecom/cable names such as CHTR to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a ≥4% one-day gain from within 5% of the 52-week low with volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average. Backtest it first, since it is a falling-knife setup.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Oct 14 catalyst. Coverage points to an AI-cloud/software rebound: NetApp–Oracle OCI storage news, easing OpenAI revenue worries, and a Mizuho top pick. Those reports are dated Oct 13, so the attribution is uncertain.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ORCL is a mega-cap enterprise software/AI-cloud name that no strategy includes. The move was also a sector and news-sentiment rebound rather than a clean gap or earnings event, so a momentum or news-reactive filter would have been weak on it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap AI/cloud names (ORCL, plus peers like MSFT, NOW and CRM) to the momentum strategy's universe, gated by a sector-breadth trigger (e.g. ≥60% of the group up >2% by 10:30 ET). Test that first in the backtest.

top_movers.catalyst: No single news event found for Oct 14. Likely continuation of a rally on analyst target raises (Morgan Stanley $100, Benchmark $105), the $4.3B Food Ingredients sale to CVC, and the buyback, ahead of Q3 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: IFF is a ~$22B mid/large-cap specialty chemicals/ingredients name. With no discrete catalyst, the move was a gradual drift toward the 52-week high ($89.32), which gap-up or news-reactive filters wouldn't flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap materials/staples names such as IFF to the momentum-trader universe, with a trigger on a close within 2% of the 52-week high plus analyst target raises. Test the effect on position count first.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for 2026-10-14; likely a natural gas price rally lifting gas producers. Next earnings are Oct 27, so this isn't earnings-driven.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EXE (Expand Energy) is a ~$22B mid/large-cap natural gas E&P that no strategy lists. With no news catalyst, a sector-beta move gave news-reactive and momentum filters nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a nat-gas E&P group (EXE, AR, RRC, CRK) to the momentum universe, entered when the group's average daily move is ≥ +3% and NG=F is up, so sector rallies get caught without needing a company headline.

top_movers.catalyst: Chip-equipment profit-taking after a ~80% YTD run. AMAT gave no industry spending forecast at its investor day, and China/geopolitical worries added to the selling. LRCX and KLA fell about 4%. Date matching is uncertain.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AMAT is a ~$370B large-cap semi-equipment name that no strategy lists. The drop was a gradual sector de-rating (sixth straight down day) with no gap or catalyst, and a long-only bot has no use for it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semi-equipment names (AMAT, LRCX, KLA) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a sector-wide drop of 4% or more plus RSI(2) below 10, so the bot can buy sector-wide profit-taking dips.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-14; searches turned up nothing dated that day. Likely an AI-infrastructure / tech sector pullback or profit-taking after a big run.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: FLEX is a mid/large-cap EMS/hardware contract manufacturer (Nasdaq, Singapore-domiciled) that no strategy lists. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive filter would not have fired either.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for a long-only bot; the move is sector beta with no event. If wanted, add AI-hardware supply-chain names like FLEX to the momentum universe, gated on a ≥5% single-day drop with ≥1.5× average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Q3 earnings reported Oct 13 (EPS $2.59 beat, guidance raised). Shares still fell about 5% on a large talc-litigation charge and a MedTech revenue miss tied to Middle East disruption. Press coverage of the reaction conflicts.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: JNJ is a mega-cap defensive pharma/healthcare name that no strategy includes. The drop was also an earnings gap that appeared at the open, so momentum and mean-reversion filters would have had no pre-gap signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap healthcare to the news-reactive strategy's universe, with an earnings-gate release for names gapping ≤ -4% on a results day. That would allow a mean-reversion long after the drop when guidance was raised. Otherwise, no change.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely Q3 2026 results reported Oct 13: U.S. same-store sales rose only 0.3% (vs +5.2% a year ago), intl +0.2%, so the stock fell on weak comps. I couldn't find an article dated Oct 14 that confirms this.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DPZ is a mid-cap restaurant franchisor that no strategy includes. The drop also looks like a post-earnings gap lower, and a long-only bot would skip it or its earnings gate would block it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add mid-cap consumer-discretionary and restaurant names like DPZ to the news-reactive universe, and let the earnings gate release names with a post-results gap of -4% or worse as mean-reversion watchlist candidates.
